text: A separate Python microservice extracted from the tatara, magic-trainer and ros2 Claude Code wrapper methodology.
Compatible with the ~/Documents/workbench project (workbench plugin flow runs inside a session).
Implemented following the plugin TDD methodology, with a fake claude end-to-end test of the full lifecycle.
README.md covering the functionality: endpoints, methods, bodies, SSE events and hooks.
Container and docker-compose with volumes for workdir and past sessions.
Configurable with config.yaml: initialisation details, prompts, mise tooling, plugin pre-install.
Definable hooks: onCreate, onTurn, onDestroy, onAgentResponse, onAgentToolCall and the rest of the event set.
Analyze the source projects to see what Claude Code functionality is used and how (docs/source-analysis.md).
Service configuration wraps the known Claude Code env vars as typed fields, with extra passthrough, per-session override and redaction.
Documentation covers service configuration: every config.yaml key with type, default and mapped env var, with examples.
HTTP API for sessions, turns, interrupt, transcript and event streaming (SSE plus polling), with auth and metrics.
The backend drives interactive claude under a PTY, not the Agent SDK and not -p.
DELETE /v1/sessions/{id} keeps the session dir and the workdir by default; only ?purge=true deletes them, and a mounted workdir is never deleted.

AskUserQuestion is forwarded by default: the PreToolUse relay denies it with guidance and emits a question event, and the question event envelope is also POSTed (signed with server.callback_secret) to the turn's callbackUrl, else the session's callbackUrl. The API uses camelCase callbackUrl consistently in request bodies, turn records and snapshots.
docker-compose.yml declares a third named volume mise mounted at /opt/mise next to workdir and sessions.

onTurnComplete fires for every terminal turn state (completed, failed, interrupted, timeout) with state in its data; turn completion callbacks follow the same rule. Orchestrator call, the user did not object.

Trust model: one wrapper instance per project or assignment; bearer-token callers are fully trusted. No workdir allowlist and no callback host policy. The service must not be exposed to untrusted callers, and the README says so.
Per-session secret env overrides are never persisted; resuming such a session requires resending them in the resume request body.
User (mid-run): make the service installable through pip as a package exposing a command on PATH, runnable in a Dockerfile or on an existing containerless installation.
